rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: build a local routine and support circle within a month [Action]
rows.description: The person finds a regular tiffin service, joins a weekend hobby group and saves emergency numbers of a doctor and a landlord. A small local network turns a strange city into a manageable one.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, impulsive action, means-end analysis, mental simulation, negotiation, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: choose the cheapest option without checking safety [Pitfall]
rows.description: To save money, the person picks a very low-rent room in an unlit area with poor locks. Cost dominates the decision, and safety problems soon force another move.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, forward planning, means-end analysis, mental simulation, negotiation, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
rows.subtype: Approach: two-week trial stay before a long lease [Revision]
rows.description: Unsure of the area, the person takes a short-term room first, learns commute times and neighbours, and only then signs a longer lease elsewhere. A trial cuts the cost of a wrong choice.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, forward planning, impulsive action, means-end analysis, mental simulation, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: gather information from a qualified doctor [Action]
rows.description: After a persistent symptom, a young worker books an appointment, writes down when it started and what makes it worse, and asks what tests are needed. Going to a professional replaces guesswork from social media.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, contingency planning, forward planning, inversion, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: search symptoms online and assume the worst [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person reads forums late at night, matches the symptoms to a serious illness and stops sleeping. Catastrophic thinking grows without facts and delays a proper visit.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, contingency planning, forward planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: avoid the appointment hoping it will pass [Pitfall]
rows.description: Busy with a project and afraid of bad news, the person keeps postponing the check-up for weeks. Avoidance feels safe short term, but delays treatment and adds stress.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, forward planning, inversion, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: prepare questions and bring a family member [Action]
rows.description: The person writes questions for the consultation and asks a sibling to come along to listen and note the doctor's words. A second pair of ears helps when anxiety makes it hard to remember details.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, contingency planning, forward planning, inversion, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: plan around the results with scenarios [Thinking]
rows.description: While waiting for lab reports, the person thinks through two paths, a mild finding and a serious one, and lists what would follow, including leave from work and insurance claims. Contingency thinking lowers uncertainty without predicting the result.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, inversion, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: second opinion when advice is unclear [Revision]
rows.description: When the first explanation feels rushed and the options are large, the person asks for records and consults another specialist before deciding. Seeking a second view corrects for one source being wrong or incomplete.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, contingency planning, forward planning, inversion

rows.subtype: Approach: check the health insurance and work leave rules [Action]
rows.description: The person reads the policy for waiting periods and covered procedures, and asks HR about medical leave. Knowing the practical side early avoids financial surprises during treatment.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, forward planning, inversion, seeking advice
